(ou: por que o russo nunca confunde ir a: (or: why Russian never confuses going on foot with going by vehicle, nor going right now in a straight line with going back and forth every day)
Em português «ir» serve para tudo. Em ru: In English "go" does everything (and you add "on foot" or "by bus" if you need to). In Russian, verbs of motion come in TWO verbs for each idea. The determinate verb describes an action that is happening now, in a single direction: «идти», «ехать». The indeterminate verb describes a habit, a round trip or an ability: «ходить», «ездить». On top of that, Russian separates the MEANS: on foot (идти / ходить) versus by transport (ехать / ездить). Guiding question: am I going now, in one direction (идти / ехать)? Or is it a habit, a round trip or an ability (ходить / ездить)? In the past, «ходил» can mean "went and came back". With means of transport you use «на» + prepositional: на автобусе, на метро, на машине.
em português o mesmo «ir» serve para a p: in English the same "go" serves for walking, for the bus, for now or for every day ("I go to work by bus"). Russian chooses the verb by the means and by the situation.
I am walking to the shop (now).
I go to the shop every day (habit).
He is on his way to work (now).
He goes to work by bus (always).
A habit calls for the indeterminate: ходить.

Verbos de movimento: duas perguntas, tab: Verbs of motion: two questions, the table of the 4 verbs and the prefixes
PASSO 1: As duas perguntas que o russo f: STEP 1: The two questions Russian asks before saying "to go". In English the verb "go" does it all: "I go to the baker's on foot", "I'm flying to Moscow", "I'm going to work now" and "I go to work every day". In Russian you can never use one verb for those four sentences! Before speaking, Russian asks two questions. • 1. Question 1: ON FOOT or BY VEHICLE? If you use your own legs, you use the pair ИДТИ́ / ХОДИ́ТЬ. If wheels or rails are involved (a car, a bus, a train, even to another city or country!), you use the pair Е́ХАТЬ / Е́ЗДИТЬ. Flying and sailing have their own pairs, ЛЕТЕ́ТЬ / ЛЕТА́ТЬ and ПЛЫТЬ / ПЛА́ВАТЬ, but for a trip in general, whatever the transport, Russians also say Е́ХАТЬ / Е́ЗДИТЬ. • 2. Question 2: ONE DIRECTION NOW (an arrow →) or ROUND TRIP / HABIT (⇄)? One-way (→ ИДТИ́ / Е́ХАТЬ): you are moving in a single direction toward a specific destination (now or in a specific plan). Multi-directional (⇄ ХОДИ́ТЬ / Е́ЗДИТЬ): repeated movement (a round-trip routine: every day, often), movement with no fixed direction (strolling around town) or, in the past, a completed round trip (Вчера́ я ходи́л в кино́ = Yesterday I went to the cinema and I am already back!). STEP 2: The master table of the 4 verbs of motion. The golden secret of the past: in Russian, saying Вчера́ я ходи́л(а) в музе́й (on foot) or В про́шлом году́ мы е́здили в Росси́ю (by vehicle or plane) is exactly the same as saying Вчера́ я был(а́) в музе́е / Мы бы́ли в Росси́и: you went there and you are already back! STEP 3: The 5 spatial prefixes of motion (ПО-, ПРИ-, У-, В-, ВЫ-). When we put a spatial prefix in front of the verbs of motion, we show the exact direction of the action. STEP 4: Summary chart: verbs of motion.

Prefixos de direção e o futuro com по-: Direction prefixes and the future with по-
Os verbos de movimento aceitam prefixos: Motion verbs take prefixes that show direction: при- (arrive), у- (leave, go away), в- (go in), вы- (go out). On foot: приходить, уходить, входить, выходить. By vehicle: приезжать, уезжать, въезжать, выезжать. The prefix «по-» makes the perfective of «идти» and «ехать»: «пойти» and «поехать». They are used for the future («Завтра я пойду в магазин» = tomorrow I will go to the shop) and to say that someone has set off («Я поехал на работу» = I have left for work). Past tense: пошёл, пошла, пошли; поехал, поехала, поехали.
Para o futuro use «по-» + forma conjugad: For the future use «по-» + a conjugated form (пойду), never the bare infinitive.
Com transporte use «приезжать» (приходит: With a vehicle use «приезжать» (приходить is on foot).
